Hi Maya — thanks for the sample and good questions. Short answers up front: portal preferred; email fallback accepted with strict subject-token and searchable PDF; support UTF-8. More details below.

1) Routing token / subject line
- Preferred: use the vendor account token + PO number in the subject. Example subject we can parse automatically: 
  Invoice | RedwoodAcct: SUNNYSIDE | PO: 12345 | INV: SS-987
- If your system can't add the token, PO alone is acceptable but will route to a manual queue which delays processing.

2) Character set / OCR
- We process PDFs with UTF-8 / Unicode text reliably. if a PDF is a scanned image (TIFF embed), our OCR can fail especially for accented characters unless the scanned image is high-DPI and uses Latin-1-compatible fonts.
- Best practice: generate a searchable PDF (embedded text) or embed fonts in the PDF. If you must send scanned pages, please ensure 300 DPI minimum and avoid TIFF containers inside the PDF.

3) Multi-PO invoices
- Preferred: one invoice per PDF tied to a single PO (simpler and faster). If you send a single invoice covering multiple POs, include all PO numbers in the subject token separated by semicolons, e.g., PO: 12345;12346. We'll attempt automatic split but it increases manual verification.

4) Attachments and structure
- One invoice per PDF file. If you have supplemental CSV/CSV-like lineitem exports, include them as a separate attachment (CSV, UTF-8). For large line item descriptions that contain commas, prefer pipe (|) as delimiter.

5) Example minimal subject and filename conventions to avoid parsing errors:
  Subject: Invoice | RedwoodAcct: SUNNYSIDE | PO: 12345 | INV: SS-987
  Filename: SUNNYSIDE_INV_SS-987_PO12345.pdf

6) Next steps
- If you can, please resubmit the redacted sample as a searchable PDF (or attach a CSV of the line items).
- I'll copy our AP intake engineer (Kim) on details in case we need a one-time parser tweak for special characters.

Hi Maya — thanks for the follow-ups and for being flexible on the temporary workaround. A couple of clarifications from our side so your ops team can implement quickly: 

- CSV fallback: yes, we will accept a separate UTF-8 CSV named lineitems.csv alongside the scanned PDF for a limited pilot period. Please make the CSV a single-level file with the following column headers exactly: InvoiceNumber, PO, LineNumber, Description, Quantity, UnitPrice, Currency. Use pipe (|) as the delimiter if your descriptions contain commas.

- Filename restrictions: avoid control characters and non-printable glyphs. Em dashes and parentheses are allowed, but keep filenames under 120 characters. Prefer ASCII-only filenames if possible to reduce SFTP/ingestion edge cases.

- Subject parsing for multiple POs: use semicolon-separated list, no spaces after semicolons, e.g.: PO: 12345;12346;12348

- OCR/charset guidance recap: embedded text (searchable PDF) > embedded fonts > scanned image (300 DPI min). If you have trouble generating embedded fonts, export as PDF/A where possible.

I'll escalate the sample you attach to our parser team (Kim) — Kim, can you confirm if we need a one-off mapping for Sunnyside's ERP export?

Thanks — once we get a corrected sample (searchable PDF or scanned PDF + lineitems.csv) we'll push the vendor live for automatic ingestion.
